headline_marked: GM's AI agents [[tripled merged pull requests]] by redesigning engineering workflows
headline: GM's AI agents tripled merged pull requests by redesigning engineering workflows
summary: GM's autonomous driving division now uses AI agents to accelerate 85% of engineering tasks beyond coding, leading to faster releases and fewer defects.
details: General Motors' autonomous driving division now spends only 15% of engineering time writing code. AI agents handle the remaining 85% of tasks, including analyzing vehicle data, triaging problems, running experiments, and testing potential fixes.

This shift has resulted in roughly three times as many merged pull requests across GM’s autonomous vehicle engineering organization. It also leads to faster releases and fewer defects escaping into later stages of development.

GM achieved these gains by completely redesigning engineering workflows around AI agents, rather than just adding AI coding assistants. This approach addresses the broader inefficiencies in the development process beyond code writing.

The company divided its autonomous vehicle work into several loops: developing and testing software in simulation, testing vehicles on public roads, and monitoring vehicles after they reach customers. They then identified and automated the longest bottleneck in each loop.

GM connected agents to internal tools and petabytes of company data through customized Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers. They also created version-controlled "skills," which are instruction documents that tell agents how to perform specific tasks.

One high-value application involves agents analyzing telemetry data from public road vehicles, conducting initial triage, and creating issues for engineers. Agents can also call underlying tools directly, rather than relying on graphical interfaces.

The output from agents is designed to be human-readable, identifying potential problems, locating affected components, and providing supporting historical data. Agent permissions are based on those of the engineer using them, ensuring accountability.

Background agents also run machine-learning experiments in parallel, executing tests and collecting results based on engineer-defined parameters. GM treated its internal agent platform as a product, with dedicated engineers helping teams adopt and optimize workflows.
